world_facts.name: The Society
world_facts.description: A hierarchical governing power that suppresses the Red population, controlling distribution and enforcing a meritocracy based on birth.

world_facts.name: The Secret Garden
world_facts.description: A hidden facility on Mars containing plants, insects, and a view of the sky, likely used by the Grays, which Darrow and Eo discover.

world_facts.name: Spiderworms
world_facts.description: Genetically engineered creatures used to knit silk within the mining structures.

summary: The chapter opens with Darrow witnessing the unfair distribution of Laurels to Gamma, a system designed by the Society to keep the Red population subservient. Darrow struggles with suppressed rage, but his wife, Eo, diverts his anger through dance. Following the ceremony, Eo leads Darrow through hidden, dangerous tunnels to a secret garden located within a restricted facility. In this place, which features real plants and insects—things Darrow has only ever seen on screens—they share an intimate moment under a transparent dome that reveals the night sky. While in the garden, Eo pushes Darrow to adopt her vision of rebellion against the Golds, urging him to use his influence to fight for the land they mine, which she believes belongs to their people. Darrow, still haunted by the loss of his father to a failed uprising, rejects her call to action, arguing that life and family are more important than ideological martyrdom. Despite their conflicting philosophies, they watch the sunrise together before returning to the industrial gray of the mines. Upon exiting the secret passage into the Webbery, their emotional interlude is shattered when an oily voice from Earth confronts them, suggesting they have been discovered in the restricted area, setting up immediate danger for the couple.
